name: Hopp
summary: Business travel management from Bolt, branded Hopp: book and control company rides from one dashboard, with per-person and per-group spend limits, automated ride reports, expensing integrations and a single consolidated monthly invoice. No activation cost and no minimum commitment — you pay per ride.
best_for: teams that already travel by ride-hailing and want the spend on one invoice with per-person limits instead of expense claims
skip_if: your team travels where Bolt has thin driver coverage, or you need a published per-ride rate card to budget against
honest_knock: The honest note is that the platform is free and the rides are not. Hopp Business charges no activation fee and no minimum commitment, so the whole cost is ride pricing, which moves with city, vehicle class and demand — and coverage thins out wherever Bolt does not already run. Check both on your own routes before you move a travel budget across.

pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-09-23 on gethopp.com/en/business/) Hopp Business publishes no subscription price because it does not charge one: the page states there are no activation costs and no minimum commitment, and billing is per ride on a single consolidated monthly invoice. Ride fares vary by city, vehicle class and demand and are not published as a rate card. The site cites 50,000+ businesses; the equivalent Bolt for Business page cited over 70,000 companies when read on 2 September 2026. The gethopp.com homepage says Hopp is brought to you by Bolt Technology OU and cites the group's 50+ countries on 5 continents; neither page lists the cities where Hopp Business itself runs.

compare_with.name: Uber for Business
compare_with.why: the obvious comparison, and it turns on coverage — check which of the two actually has drivers in the cities your team travels to, because that decides more than the dashboard does
